title: Harborlight Adoption: Staff Onboarding Brief
customer_attendees: Marta Diaz - Head of Data Platforms
header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Record: Enabled
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Holloway (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Jonas Park (Redwood SE), Marta Diaz (Harborlight), Liam O'Neal (Harborlight), Ruchi Patel (Harborlight), Omar Farouk (Harborlight)
summary: Kickoff and onboarding brief to align Harborlight's initial implementation: authentication and networking design choices (SAML SSO, VPC peering), minimal pilot success criteria, timeline for runbook delivery, and an ops/roles handoff. SE-led portion covered Private deployment checklist and a quick perf baseline plan. Security asked about audit logs/KMS and data residency. Agreed next deliverables: runbook draft, pricing summary, pilot scope doc, and scheduling a benchmarking session in two weeks.
topics: Network topology: VPC peering vs private link
transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll kick off in a minute, we have Marcus and Priya from our side who'll walk through the ops runbook and security checklist.
[00:16] Marta (Harborlight): Hi all, thanks. We wanted to make sure we focus on onboarding for the trading analytics pilot - low latency, high throughput, and strict residency.
[00:30] Marcus (SE): Great, Marcus here. I'll start with a quick architecture overview. We're proposing Redwood Private in your VPC, with a customer-managed control plane. That gives you audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:46] Liam (Harborlight): Quick question - do we need VPC peering or can we use PrivateLink? We have policies that limit peering across prod accounts.
[00:59] Jonas (SE): Good point. Either works. PrivateLink avoids cross-account peering but may add some egress cost and slight latency. For our past customers, we saw ~3-7 ms extra tail latency on PrivateLink vs peering for short sequences. Those numbers are from internal benchmarks, your workload might differ.
[01:18] Ruchi (Harborlight): Are those benchmarks with KV cache enabled? Our model usage will rely heavily on KV cache for inference.
[01:26] Marcus (SE): Yes, the baseline included KV caching for prefix reuse. We'll include a bench matrix for long and short context.
[01:33] Omar (Harborlight): On security: KMS, HSM, can Redwood integrate with our HSM? We have an on-prem HSM for key custody.
[01:44] Avery (AE): We support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we also have a plugin path for customer HSMs via the private control plane but that is part of the Private deployment offering. We can flag it as a requirements item.
[01:59] Marta: Also SOC2 reports. Do you have recent attestations?
[02:06] Priya (CSM): Yes we'll share the SOC2 Type II and ISO summary. I'll drop the security packet after the call.
[02:13] Liam: Timeline - we're aiming to cut the pilot in 4 weeks. Is that realistic?
[02:20] Jonas: For a minimal pilot (single model, one inference route, small dataset) 3-4 weeks is reasonable. If you want HSM integration or on-prem HSM proof, plan for additional time—possibly 6-8 weeks, because of procurement and network approvals.
[02:38] Marta: Success criteria - we want 95th percentile latency under 120 ms for typical prompts and cost per 1k tokens under a threshold - we have a target, we'll share the number.
[02:49] Marcus: We'll create an initial runbook with per-route SLOs and recommended batching/quantization settings. That will be in the deliverables.
[02:58] Ruchi: Who will own the operational alerts? We want to tie into PagerDuty and CloudWatch.
[03:05] Priya: Ops ownership is shared at first: Redwood will provide alerting integration and we'll operate during the pilot. Post-pilot we can hand off runbook and escalation steps.
[03:14] Omar: Audit logs - retention policy? We need 1 year of immutable logs for compliance.
[03:21] Marcus: We can configure audit log retention to your retention policy and ship to your S3 bucket or log ingestion endpoint. Immutable retention will depend on your object storage lifecycle rules.
[03:30] Speaker 1: (background) mm-hm mm-hm
[03:36] Avery: Quick demo segment - Marcus do you want to share the quick dashboard for model routes?
[03:43] Marcus: Yep screen share now. 
[03:50] [screen share noise] 
[04:02] Marcus: This is the Console - you can see per-route token costs, tail latency, and error percentages. For the pilot we'll create a route for the trading-qa model with canary rollout enabled so we can test fallbacks to a small L2 model if latency spikes.
[04:21] Liam: About canaries - does that incur double cost during a rollout?
[04:26] Jonas: There is some duplication but we can control the percentage and time window; typically cost delta is small if you keep canary traffic under 5-10% and short windows. We'll document expected overhead.
[04:40] Ruchi: For service accounts and RBAC—how granular? We need per-team keys and role separation.
[04:47] Priya: We support SSO and SCIM provisioning so you can map groups to roles. We'll work with your IAM team for role mappings.
[04:56] Omar: Data residency - this pilot must run in the us-east-1 region and not cross other regions.
[05:02] Marcus: Noted. Private deployment can be pinned to region and to a dedicated capacity pool on the region of choice.
[05:10] Marta: Procurement - what's the contract lead time for Private?
[05:15] Avery: For Private it's mostly a platform license plus implementation services; contract turnaround typically 2-3 weeks, depending on legal review. We have standard language for security addenda.
[05:25] Liam: Any competitor caveats we should be aware of? We're also evaluating BigCloudAI's managed endpoints.
[05:32] Jonas: BigCloudAI is fine for simple endpoints but they often don't provide the same level of per-token cost breakdown or the continuous KV-cache optimizations we do; also their private deployment requires more infra effort.
[05:42] Marta: Can you send a sample runbook and pilot scope doc?
[05:47] Priya: Absolutely - we'll deliver: 1) pilot scope, 2) runbook draft, 3) pricing summary and expected cost overheads, 4) security packet. Expect these in 3 business days.
[05:59] Ruchi: Benchmarks - can you run a small perf test with our model (we'll provide a sanitized snapshot)?
[06:06] Marcus: Yes, we'll run a sprint bench. Please provide model artifact and sample prompts. We'll schedule the benchmark session for two weeks from today.
[06:17] Marta: Great. Any blockers on our side? We'll need network approvals for PrivateLink, IAM group mapping, and procurement signoff.
[06:27] Avery: We'll document those dependencies in the pilot scope.
[06:33] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[06:40] Jonas: Quick recap - Marcus will own the runbook draft, Priya will send security docs and pricing, Avery will coordinate contract/legal intro, and we'll schedule the perf bench.
[06:51] Avery: Any final questions?
[06:55] Omar: One more - log redaction: can Redwood redact PII from logs before they hit our S3?
[07:02] Marcus: We have configurable log filters; we can apply regex-based redaction or explicit redaction hooks in the private control plane. We'll validate with your security team.
[07:14] Marta: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the docs.
[07:18] Priya: Thanks, we'll follow up with dates and a calendar invite for the bench.
[07:25] [00:00:00] call end
